Berwal falls short after spirited fight



India's best-ever boxing campaign



NEW DELHI: India's Narender Berwal fell just short of winning the Commonwealth Games boxing title, but the heavyweight boxer has already shifted his focus to the Asian Games. After settling for silver in the men's 90+kg category, Berwal promised to come back stronger and make up for the missed opportunity.Berwal lost to England's Damar Thomas in the final but said the defeat has only motivated him to work harder for the next major event."I missed out by a narrow margin, but I will try to make up for it at the Asian Games. I gave my best; it was a tough fight against the English opponent, and I missed the win by a whisker. I'll make up for it at the Asian Games," Berwal said."We performed much better than we had anticipated. Boxers like Sumit Kundu, Aditya Yadav, Parveen Hooda, and Kapil Pokhariya lost very close 3-2 bouts. We could have potentially won 14 out of 14 medals. Those four boxers lost by the narrowest of margins. You will see great results in the upcoming Asian Games. We will prepare thoroughly and give our best," the Indian boxer said.Berwal produced a determined performance in the gold medal bout but was beaten by Damar Thomas through a unanimous 5-0 decision.Despite missing the top prize, the Indian heavyweight finished on the podium with a silver medal and capped off an impressive campaign in Glasgow.Berwal's silver helped India complete its most successful Commonwealth Games boxing campaign.The Indian boxing team finished on top of the medal standings with a record 10 medals - seven gold and three silver.
Article Summary: India's Narender Berwal settles for silver in the men's 90+kg category. Berwal lost to England's Damar Thomas in the final but said the defeat has only motivated him to work harder for the next major event. India finished on top of the medal standings with a record 10 medals - seven gold and three silver.

Article Title: 0-5 down, gold at the end: How boxer Ankush Panghal turned the tide to win CWG title
Article Text:
Ankush Panghal (PTI Photo)

How Panghal completed the comeback



Perfect campaign in Glasgow



Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India records its best-ever boxing campaign



India's Ankush Panghal produced one of the biggest comebacks of the Commonwealth Games 2026 boxing competition, recovering from a 5-0 deficit after the opening round to defeat England's Dimeji Shittu and win the men's 80kg gold medal on Saturday.The 22-year-old from Haryana stayed calm after a tough start and fought back brilliantly to register a 4-1 split-decision victory. His gold helped India finish with its best-ever boxing campaign at the Commonwealth Games.After the win, Panghal admitted he felt the pressure after losing the first round but never stopped believing."It feels great to have won the gold medal. But during the bout, my morale took a bit of a hit. I was down 5-0 in the first round, so I felt some pressure... but I managed to win the bout somehow. I also want to thank those who came to support me. This medal is for them... I'm dedicating the medal to my entire family and the whole of India," Panghal said after winning the gold medal.Shittu made the stronger start and dominated the opening round with aggressive attacks. Panghal, however, slowly found his rhythm with smart movement, sharp backhand punches and disciplined defence.The momentum completely changed in the later stages as the Indian boxer controlled the contest. Shittu was also handed a point deduction, and Panghal finished the bout as the stronger boxer to earn the judges' decision despite the home crowd backing the Englishman.The Army boxer remained composed throughout and became India's seventh boxing gold medallist of the Games.Panghal enjoyed an outstanding tournament from start to finish. Before the final, he recorded unanimous victories over Zalaan Jan (Antigua and Barbuda), Jade Micock (Seychelles) and Joshua Ofori (Canada).He then capped off his unbeaten run with his memorable comeback victory over Shittu in the gold medal bout.India produced its finest-ever boxing performance at the Commonwealth Games, winning seven gold medals and three silver medals.The women's team led the charge with five gold medals. Jaismine Lamboria (57kg), Preeti Pawar (54kg), Priya Ghanghas (60kg), Sakshi Chaudhary (51kg) and Arundhati Choudhary (70kg) all won their finals. Olympic medallist Lovlina Borgohain (75kg) settled for silver.In the men's events, Sachin Siwach (60kg) joined Panghal as a gold medallist, while Jadumani Singh (55kg) and Narender Berwal (+90kg) won silver.India's previous best boxing performance at the Commonwealth Games came at Gold Coast 2018, where the country won seven medals, including three gold.
Article Summary: Ankush Panghal won the men's 80kg gold medal on Saturday. The 22-year-old from Haryana fought back from a 5-0 deficit to win 4-1. His gold helped India finish with its best-ever boxing campaign at the Commonwealth Games.

India ends Day 10 with momentum

India produced its biggest day of the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games on Saturday, collecting a remarkable 16 medals to surge into fourth place in the overall standings with one day of competition remaining.A dominant display in the boxing ring, where Indian pugilists won seven gold and three silver medals, formed the backbone of the country's medal rush. The success extended beyond boxing as India added medals in para athletics, athletics and judo to take its overall tally to 39 medals, comprising 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze.India now trails only Australia, England and Canada in the medal standings. Australia continues to dominate the Games with 153 medals (62 gold, 40 silver and 51 bronze), while England sits second with 100 medals (26 gold, 40 silver and 34 bronze). Canada occupies third place with 58 medals, including 18 gold, 19 silver and 21 bronze.Indian boxing enjoyed one of its finest days in Commonwealth Games history after all 10 finalists stepped into the ring, returning with seven gold medals and three silver medals.The seven golds and three silvers capped a flawless campaign for the Indian contingent, with every boxer who reached Friday's semi-finals progressing to a medal-winning finish.India celebrated a one-two finish in the men's F57 shot put as Soman Rana and Shubham Juyal occupied the top two places.Rana clinched gold with a season-best effort of 13.40 metres, finishing 0.12 metres ahead of compatriot Juyal, whose own season-best throw of 13.28 metres earned silver. Cameroon's Cedric Azamdzi completed the podium with a best mark of 12.57 metres.The result gave India another memorable double podium during an outstanding day across multiple disciplines.India added two more athletics medals in the men's triple jump.Praveen Chithravel secured silver with a best leap of 16.58 metres, finishing just 0.14 metres behind Jamaica's Jordan Scott, who claimed gold with 16.72 metres.Selva Prabhu Thirumaran completed India's double podium by winning bronze with a jump of 16.52 metres, ensuring two Indians stood alongside Scott on the medal podium.Gulveer Singh produced one of India's standout performances on the track by winning bronze in the men's 5,000 metres.He crossed the line in 13:24.95, finishing just 0.04 seconds ahead of Kenya's Cornelius Kemboi in fourth after an intense battle over the closing metres.Australia's Ky Robinson claimed gold, while Kenya's Michael Kiplangat Kipsang took silver.The podium finish marked another landmark achievement for Indian athletics and added to Gulveer's successful Commonwealth Games campaign.India's medal tally also received a boost in judo through Unnati Sharma.Competing in the women's -63kg bronze-medal bout, Sharma defeated South Africa's Skye Knoester by Ippon in just one minute and seven seconds after executing a decisive leg hook that ended the contest immediately.The victory ensured India finished another successful day with medals spread across boxing, para athletics, athletics and judo.Saturday's remarkable haul lifted India's overall tally to 39 medals —13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze — moving the country into fourth place in the standings entering the final day of competition.While boxing accounted for 10 medals, India also celebrated podium finishes in para athletics, athletics and judo, underlining one of the country's most successful all-round performances of the Games and providing strong momentum heading into the concluding day in Glasgow.
Article Summary: India's sensational 16-medal haul, led by seven boxing golds, lifts the nation to fourth in Glasgow. Indian boxing enjoyed one of its finest days in Commonwealth Games history after all 10 finalists stepped into the ring. The success extended beyond boxing as India added medals in para athletics, athletics and judo to take its overall tally to 39.

Article Title: Gulveer Singh scripts history, becomes first Indian to win Commonwealth Games 5000m medal
Article Text:
Gulveer Singh

Gulveer Singh created history on Saturday by becoming the first Indian to win a Commonwealth Games medal in the men's 5000m and the first Indian track and field athlete to win two medals in a single edition of the Games.After winning silver in the 10,000m on July 28, the reigning Asian champion added a bronze in the 5000m, finishing in 13:24.95 on the final day of the athletics competition.Kenya's Mathew Kipchumba Kipsang won the gold in 13:23.61, while Australia's Ky Robinson, who had earlier taken the 10,000m gold, claimed silver in 13:24.70.The 28-year-old Indian, who holds the national records in both the 5000m and 10,000m, finished well outside his season's best time of 13:03.93. His timing on Saturday was also slower than his national record of 12:59.77.Gulveer stayed with the leading group throughout the race before making his move in the final lap. He edged Kenya's Cornelius Kemboi to the bronze medal by just 0.04 seconds.Kemboi, who had clocked 12:56.02 in June and is a sub-13-minute runner, finished just behind Gulveer in the race.The bronze added to Gulveer's growing list of achievements, which also includes the 10,000m bronze medal he won at the 2023 Asian Games in Hangzhou.
Article Summary: Gulveer Singh becomes first Indian to win a Commonwealth Games medal in the men's 5000m. He is also the first Indian track and field athlete to win two medals in a single edition of the Games. The 28-year-old Indian holds the national records in both the 5000m and 10,000m.

Article Title: CWG 2026: Sachin Siwach fights back to win Men's 60kg Boxing Gold, delivers India's sixth Boxing title
Article Text:
Glasgow (IANS) India’s Sachin Siwach

Ndevelo takes early advantage

Dramatic final round seals gold



India's Boxing medal winners at CWG 2026 (so far today)

Weight Category Indian Boxer Opponent Result Medal Women's 51kg Sakshi Chaudhary Ruby White (England) Won Gold Women's 54kg Preeti Pawar Scarlett Savannah Delgado (Canada) Won Gold Women's 57kg Jaismine Lamboria Michaela Walsh (Northern Ireland) Won Gold Women's 60kg Priya Ghanghas Marie-Bathoul Al-Ahmadieh (Canada) Won Gold Women's 70kg Arundhati Choudhary Chantelle Reid (England) Won Gold Men's 60kg Sachin Siwach Tryagain Morning Ndevelo (Zimbabwe) Won Gold Women's 75kg Lovlina Borgohain Emma Sue Greentree (Australia) Lost Silver Men's 55kg Jadumani Singh Jye Dixon (Australia) Lost Silver

India's Sachin Siwach produced a remarkable comeback to defeat Tryagain Morning Ndevelo and win the men's 60kg boxing gold medal at the 2026 Commonwealth Games on Saturday. Despite trailing after the opening two rounds, the Indian boxer staged a superb fightback in the final round to earn a 3-2 split decision, claiming India's sixth boxing gold medal at Glasgow 2026.The opening round was a cautious affair, with both boxers spending the early exchanges sizing each other up. Sachin looked to dictate the pace by pressing forward, while Ndevelo relied on counter-punching. A powerful late punch from the Zimbabwean proved decisive as he edged the opening round 3-2 on the judges' scorecards.The Indian increased the tempo in the second round, using his hand speed to put pressure on his opponent. However, he struggled to consistently land clean punches as Ndevelo continued to defend smartly and counter effectively.Sachin's task became tougher after the referee deducted a point for repeatedly lowering his head. Although he managed to take the second round 3-2, he still trailed heading into the decisive final three minutes.Knowing he needed a big finish, Sachin came out aggressively in the final round, relentlessly chasing Ndevelo around the ring. The Indian continued to absorb counters and received multiple warnings from the referee, but he refused to back down. His persistence paid off in the closing seconds when he landed a powerful punch that forced a standing count against Ndevelo just before the final bell. With no time left after the count, the result rested entirely with the judges.After a tense wait, Sachin was declared the winner by a 3-2 split decision, completing a stunning comeback to secure the Commonwealth Games gold medal. The triumph marked India's sixth boxing gold medal at Glasgow 2026.
Article Summary: India's Sachin Siwach produced a remarkable comeback to defeat Tryagain Morning Ndevelo and win the men's 60kg boxing gold medal at the 2026 Commonwealth Games. Sachin trailed after the opening two rounds, but staged a superb fightback in the final round to earn a 3-2 split decision. The triumph marked India's sixth boxing gold medals at Glasgow 2026.

India's Lovlina Borgohain settled for the silver medal in the women's 75kg boxing event after losing 1-4 on points to Australia's Emma-Sue Greentree in the Commonwealth Games 2026 final on Saturday.It was Lovlina's first Commonwealth Games medal and the seventh medal for India's boxing team in this edition. Along with Jadumani Singh, she is one of only two Indian boxers to finish with silver so far.Lovlina entered the ring with her left knee heavily strapped, which affected her movement in the opening round. Greentree made the better start and took the round 4-1.The Australian suffered a cut and was seen bleeding during the second round, leading to a brief stoppage. After the bout resumed, Lovlina landed a few clean punches and claimed the round 4-1.Going into the final round, three of the five judges had the contest level.The third round saw both boxers exchange punches, but Greentree edged it 4-1 to secure the gold medal.The Olympic bronze medallist had received a bye into the quarterfinals before defeating Tuvalu's Tarona Taafaki 5-0 in the semifinals to book her place in the title clash.

India continued its strong run in boxing at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow on Saturday, winning five gold medals, with Arundhati Choudhary completing the tally after beating England's Chantelle Reid in the women's 70kg final.Arundhati defeated Reid by a unanimous 5-0 decision to give India its fifth boxing gold of the competition.Earlier in the day, Jaismine Lamboria, Preeti Pawar, Sakshi Chaudhary and Priya Ghanghas had also won gold medals in their respective categories, while Jadumani Singh settled for silver.Preeti opened India's gold medal haul with a 5-0 win over Canada's Scarlett Delgado in the women's 54kg final.Reigning world champion Jaismine followed it up with another 5-0 victory against defending champion Michaela Walsh of Northern Ireland in the women's 57kg final.Sakshi then defeated England's Ruby White 5-0 in the women's 51kg final to claim India's third boxing gold of the day.Priya had a tougher contest but beat Canada's Marie-Bathoul Al-Ahmadieh 4-1 by split decision in the women's 60kg final.Jadumani missed out on gold after losing 0-5 to Australia's Jye Dixon in the men's 55kg final.
